# Dragonboat Raft audit — findings so far

Scope: captured tree `dbb02a05b62bbf7823fa3f8b5eb2ef9b949e6cc8`
(`github.com/lni/dragonboat/v3`, reports itself as v3.3.8 in
`nodehost.go:114-121`). Source is read-only; all work is in this directory.
Toolchain: go1.23.5, offline module cache. Ordinary shell has no network; tests
that listen on TCP were run through `isolated_exec`.

The reproduction tests are behind the `dragonboat_audit` build tag so the
default test run of the supplied code is unaffected. All commands below use
`-tags dragonboat_no_rocksdb,dragonboat_audit`.

Baseline evidence collected before any analysis:

- Packages must be run one at a time. The root package and
  `internal/transport` use fixed ports (250xx/260xx) and the shared
  `singleNodeHostTestDir`; `go test ./...` with default package parallelism
  makes them collide and produces spurious failures (observed: root
  `TestGossip`, `TestNodeHostIDIsStatic`, ... and `TestMessageCanBeSent`
  failing only in the parallel run). Run sequentially, both packages pass.
66:## Summary
117:## Finding 1 (executed): `INodeUser.ReadIndex` never wakes the execution engine
208:## Finding 2 (executed, minor): a candidate records a dropped ReadIndex twice
266:## Finding 3 (executed, minor): `pb.Update.HasUpdate` ignores dropped read indexes
290:## Finding 4 (executed, minor): the exported channel transport factory cannot be used
328:## Finding 5 (executed, minor): the logger cache ignores the monkey flag
350:## Finding 6 (executed): a malformed network frame crashes the NodeHost
403:## Finding 7 (executed): a short snapshot chunk crashes the receiver
424:## Finding 8 (executed, minor): a forged chunk skips validation and panics on save
472:## Finding 9 (executed): a peer message with no destination crashes the NodeHost
498:## Finding 10 (executed): a forged `Replicate` kills the node from the raft layer
572:## Finding 11 (executed): one forged `Heartbeat` kills a follower
621:## Finding 12 (executed): a peer can deliver local-only message types
659:## Finding 13 (executed): quiesce turns a leader failure into an indefinite write outage
713:## Source-based observations not reported as defects
745:## Areas reviewed without finding a defect
935:## Reproduction inventory
1041:## Fix verification
1169:## Command log (abridged)
1278:## Unresolved work

The reproduction tests are behind the `dragonboat_audit` build tag so the
default test run of the supplied code is unaffected. All commands below use
`-tags dragonboat_no_rocksdb,dragonboat_audit`.

Review roadmap:

- **Summary** - the 13 findings, one line each, with the evidence behind each.
- **Findings 1-13** - reproduction, root cause and fix sketch per finding.
- **Areas reviewed without finding a defect** - what was checked and found
  sound (quiesce, membership, linearizability, restart, leader transfer, ...).
- **Reproduction inventory** - every test/harness file and what it covers.
- **Fix verification** - the patches in `audit/diag-fixes/` and the green runs.
- **Command log / Unresolved work** - the exact commands and open points.

Fastest way to see the whole matrix (sequential, sockets needed). On this
captured tree it reports the 15 deliberate failures; the same command inside
`audit/diag-fixes/` is fully green:

```
isolated_exec: go test -p 1 -tags dragonboat_no_rocksdb,dragonboat_audit \
    . ./internal/raft ./raftpb ./logger ./internal/transport
```

Baseline evidence collected before any analysis:
1325 report.md

item.text:
The report now opens with a review roadmap so a reader can navigate it quickly.

**What I added**

A short block after the scope preamble:

- a map of the sections (summary, the 13 findings, areas reviewed without defects, reproduction inventory, fix verification, command log/unresolved work), so the 1,325-line report is easy to enter at the right level;
- the single command that produces the full matrix in one shot, with the caveat that it reports the 15 deliberate failures on this captured tree and is fully green inside `audit/diag-fixes/`.

That command is the one I actually ran for the certification, so the instructions match verified behaviour rather than the older per-test command list further down.

**State at close**

Everything else remains as verified in the previous turns: 13 findings with live reproductions and minimal fixed-copy patches, 43 audit tests (28 pass / 15 deliberate failures) reconciled across four per-package listings, evidence logs for every crash and survival, a negative-result catalogue, and every path the report cites resolving in the tree. The audited implementation is byte-identical to `../source`; all additions are build-tagged tests, harnesses, logs, the separate fixed copy and the report itself.
